source.ref: Regulation (EU) 2021/697, Article 2 (definition of 'legal entity') and Article 9(1)
source.text:
[Regulation (EU) 2021/697, Article 2, definition of 'legal entity'] ‘legal entity’ means a legal person created and recognised as such under Union, national or international law, which has legal personality and the capacity to act in its own name, exercise rights and be subject to obligations, or an entity which does not have legal personality as referred to in point (c) of Article 197(2) of the Financial Regulation;

[Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2018/1046 (the Financial Regulation that Regulation 2021/697 cites), Article 197(2)] 2. Any of the following applicants shall be eligible for participating in a call for proposals: (a) legal persons; (b) natural persons, in so far as this is required by the nature or characteristics of the action or the objective pursued by the applicant; (c) entities which do not have legal personality under the applicable national law, provided that their representatives have the capacity to undertake legal obligations on behalf of the entities and that the entities offer guarantees for the protection of the financial interests of the Union equivalent to those offered by legal persons.

rules.title: Established in the Union or an associated country
rules.reason: Your company is established in an EU Member State or an EEA EFTA state. These are the Union and an associated country of the EDF.
rules.note: The associated countries are the EEA EFTA states (under the conditions of the EEA Agreement) and, since Regulation (EU) 2025/2653, Ukraine under the conditions of the EU-Ukraine Association Agreement. That those conditions are met is not confirmed, so a company established in Ukraine is conditional here, not eligible. The EDF call documents of 2026 say: “Participation of entities established in Ukraine is pending the signature of the association agreement to EDF”, and we found no Official Journal text, Council decision or notice that says the EU-Ukraine association agreement applies to the EDF.

source.ref: Regulation (EU) 2021/697, Article 9(1) and Article 5 (as replaced by Regulation (EU) 2025/2653)
source.text:
[Regulation (EU) 2021/697, Article 9(1)] Recipients and subcontractors involved in an action shall be established in the Union or in an associated country.

[Regulation (EU) 2021/697, Article 5, as replaced by Regulation (EU) 2025/2653, Article 3(1)] The Fund shall be open to the participation of the following third countries (associated countries): (a) members of the European Free Trade Association which are members of the EEA, in accordance with the conditions laid down in the Agreement on the European Economic Area; (b) Ukraine, in accordance with the conditions laid down in the EU-Ukraine Association Agreement.

rules.title: Who may apply: contracting authorities, international organisations, SEAPs and the EDA
rules.reason: This rule applies to common procurement actions only. It is checked when you open a call of that kind.
rules.note: The call documents of the common procurement calls say the same: “be contracting authorities, international organisations, SEAPs or EDA within the meaning of Articles 11, 27(1) and 42 of the EDIP Regulation”, and that the EDA and international organisations are eligible as beneficiaries if designated as procurement agent. Article 11(3) adds that a consortium needs at least three contracting authorities from three Member States or associated countries, at least two of them contracting authorities of Member States, unless a SEAP applies alone.

source.text:
[Regulation (EU) 2025/2643, Article 11(2)] Only the following legal entities shall be eligible for common procurement actions: (a) contracting authorities of Member States or associated countries; (b) international organisations; (c) SEAPs; (d) the EDA.

[Regulation (EU) 2025/2643, Article 11(3)] Common procurement actions shall be carried out by: (a) a consortium of legal entities as referred to in paragraph 2, including at least three entities referred to in paragraph 2, point (a), from at least three Member States or associated countries of which at least two shall be contracting authorities of two Member States; or (b) a SEAP.

source.text:
[Regulation (EU) 2025/2643, Article 10(3), first sentence] For procurement carried out pursuant to Articles 11, 13 and 35 which is supported by Union funding, the cost of components originating outside the Union and associated countries shall not be higher than 35 % of the estimated cost of the components of the end product.

rules.title: Subcontractors outside the Union: the 15 to 35 % allowance
rules.reason: Common procurement under the Programme can include a subcontractor that is allocated between 15 % and 35 % of the value of the contract and is not established, or has no executive management structures, in the Union or an associated country, if a direct contractual relationship related to the defence product was established between the contractor and that subcontractor before the Regulation entered into force (it was published on 29 December 2025 and entered into force on the following day). This figure is a share of the contract value. It is not the 35 % component cost limit.
rules.note: A 'subcontractor' in the sense of this Regulation is narrower than any supplier: the definition in Article 2 requires at least 15 % of the value of the contract and a need for access to classified information, and leaves out suppliers that deliver components of their own design or production.

source.text:
[Regulation (EU) 2025/2643, Article 11(7)] By way of derogation from paragraph 6, in order to take into account industrial cooperation with non-associated third countries, common procurement that involves a subcontractor that is allocated between 15 % and 35 % of the value of the contract, and that is not established or does not have its executive management structures in the Union or in an associated country, shall be eligible for support under the Programme provided that a direct contractual relationship related to the defence product has been established between the contractor and that subcontractor prior to the date of entry into force of this Regulation.

[Regulation (EU) 2025/2643, Article 2, definition of 'subcontractor'] ‘subcontractor’ means an economic operator that is proposed by a candidate, tenderer or contractor to perform specific tasks or services under the supervision of the main contractor, contributing to the design or manufacturing of a defence product, other than what is provided by suppliers to implement the contract, for which it is allocated at least 15 % of the value of the contract, and that needs access to classified information for the performance of that contract; for the purposes of this definition, ‘supplier’ shall be understood as an economic operator that delivers components of its own design or production to the contractor.

assessments.summary: Loans to Member States for common defence procurements. A company does not apply: the rules decide whether it can be a contractor or subcontractor in a procurement that SAFE supports.

Where are your company's executive management structures established?

Does any component of your end product come from a third country that contravenes the Union's security and defence interests?

rules.title: Established in the Union, an EEA EFTA state or Ukraine
rules.reason: Say in which country your company is established, and what your role in a SAFE-supported procurement would be.
rules.note: Derogation for subcontractors: see the information line on the 15-35 % subcontractor allowance below. The paragraph binds the contractor and the 'subcontractors involved in the common procurement' of Article 16(12), who provide critical inputs, are allocated at least 15 % of the contract value and need access to classified information. A supplier below those thresholds is not bound by it.

asks.question: In a SAFE-supported procurement, would you be the contractor, a subcontractor that is allocated at least 15 % of the contract value, provides critical inputs and needs access to classified information, or another supplier?

source.ref: Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1106, Article 16(3) and Article 16(12); Article 17 and the agreement with Canada (Decision (EU) 2026/1381, Agreement Article 5(2))
source.text:
[Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1106, Article 16(3), first sentence] Contractors and subcontractors involved in the common procurement shall be established and have their executive management structures in the Union, in an EEA EFTA State or in Ukraine.

[Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1106, Article 16(12)] For the purposes of this Article, ‘subcontractors involved in the common procurement’ means any legal entity which provides critical inputs that possess unique attributes essential for the functioning of a product, which is allocated at least 15 % of the value of the contract, and which needs access to classified information for the performance of the contract.

[Council Decision (EU) 2026/1381, recital (1)] was signed on 14 February 2026, subject to its conclusion at a later date, and has been applied on a provisional basis from 13 April 2026, pending its entry into force.

[Agreement between the European Union and Canada, OJ L 2026/445, Article 5(2), first sentence] Canadian legal entities must be established in Canada and have their executive management structures in Canada, in the Union, in an EEA EFTA State, or in Ukraine.

rules.title: Executive management in the Union, an EEA EFTA state or Ukraine
rules.reason: Say where your company's executive management structures are established, and what your role in a SAFE-supported procurement would be.
rules.note: Paragraph 8 also requires the infrastructure, facilities, assets and resources used for the procurement to be located in a Member State, an EEA EFTA state or Ukraine, with a narrow exception where no alternative is readily available. This service does not ask about that. The paragraph binds the contractor and the 'subcontractors involved in the common procurement' of Article 16(12), who provide critical inputs, are allocated at least 15 % of the contract value and need access to classified information. A supplier below those thresholds is not bound by it.

asks.question: In a SAFE-supported procurement, would you be the contractor, a subcontractor that is allocated at least 15 % of the contract value, provides critical inputs and needs access to classified information, or another supplier?
Where are your company's executive management structures established?

source.text:
[Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1106, Article 16(3), first sentence] Contractors and subcontractors involved in the common procurement shall be established and have their executive management structures in the Union, in an EEA EFTA State or in Ukraine.

[Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1106, Article 16(12)] For the purposes of this Article, ‘subcontractors involved in the common procurement’ means any legal entity which provides critical inputs that possess unique attributes essential for the functioning of a product, which is allocated at least 15 % of the value of the contract, and which needs access to classified information for the performance of the contract.

[Council Decision (EU) 2026/1381, recital (1)] was signed on 14 February 2026, subject to its conclusion at a later date, and has been applied on a provisional basis from 13 April 2026, pending its entry into force.

rules.title: Not controlled by a third country other than an EEA EFTA state or Ukraine
rules.reason: Say whether your company is controlled by a country or an entity outside the EU, the EEA EFTA states and Ukraine, and what your role in a SAFE-supported procurement would be. If you do not know, find out who your ultimate owners are.
rules.note: Paragraph 6 of Article 16 lists what the guarantees must show. The paragraph binds the contractor and the 'subcontractors involved in the common procurement' of Article 16(12), who provide critical inputs, are allocated at least 15 % of the contract value and need access to classified information. A supplier below those thresholds is not bound by it.

asks.question: In a SAFE-supported procurement, would you be the contractor, a subcontractor that is allocated at least 15 % of the contract value, provides critical inputs and needs access to classified information, or another supplier?

source.text:
[Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1106, Article 16(3), second sentence] They shall not be subject to control by a third country which is not an EEA EFTA State or Ukraine or by another third-country entity which is not established in the Union, in an EEA EFTA State or in Ukraine.

[Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1106, Article 16(5), first sentence] By way of derogation from paragraph 3, a legal entity established in the Union and controlled by another third country or by another third-country entity may participate in the common procurement if it has been subject to screening within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2019/452 and, where necessary, to appropriate mitigation measures, or if it provides guarantees verified by the Member State in which the contractor or subcontractor involved in the common procurement is established.

[Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1106, Article 16(12)] For the purposes of this Article, ‘subcontractors involved in the common procurement’ means any legal entity which provides critical inputs that possess unique attributes essential for the functioning of a product, which is allocated at least 15 % of the value of the contract, and which needs access to classified information for the performance of the contract.

rules.title: Components from outside the Union, the EEA EFTA states and Ukraine: at most 35 % of component cost
rules.reason: Give the share of the estimated cost of the components of your end product that originates outside the Union, the EEA EFTA states and Ukraine.
rules.note: The percentage is measured against the estimated cost of the components of the end product, not against the contract value. It is a property of the end product you would supply, so the answer is about one product.
rules.denominator: the estimated cost of the components of the end product

asks.question: What share of the estimated cost of the components of your end product originates outside the EU, the EEA EFTA states and Ukraine?

source.text:
[Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1106, Article 16(10), first sentence] The cost of components originating outside the Union, EEA EFTA States and Ukraine shall not be higher than 35 % of the estimated cost of the components of the end product.

[Council Decision (EU) 2026/1381, recital (1)] was signed on 14 February 2026, subject to its conclusion at a later date, and has been applied on a provisional basis from 13 April 2026, pending its entry into force.

[Agreement between the European Union and Canada, OJ L 2026/445, Article 5(8), first sentence] The cost of components originating in Canada may exceed 35 % of the estimated cost of the components of the end product.

rules.title: No component from a third country that contravenes the Union's security and defence interests
rules.reason: Say whether any component comes from a third country that contravenes the security and defence interests of the Union and its Member States. The regulation gives no list of such countries; if you are unsure, ask the contracting authority.
rules.note: This is a separate rule from the 35 % threshold. It is a yes or no, with no percentage.

asks.question: Does any component of your end product come from a third country that contravenes the Union's security and defence interests?

source.text: [Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1106, Article 16(10), second sentence] For the purpose of procurements supported by the SAFE instrument, no component shall be sourced from a third country that contravenes the security and defence interests of the Union and its Member States.

rules.title: Subcontractors outside the Union: the 15 to 35 % allowance
rules.reason: A procurement can include a subcontractor that is allocated between 15 % and 35 % of the value of the contract and is not established, or has no executive management structures, in the Union, an EEA EFTA state or Ukraine, if at least one of two conditions is met: a direct contractual relationship related to the defence product existed between the contractor and that subcontractor before this Regulation entered into force (it was published on 28 May 2025 and entered into force on the following day, 29 May 2025), or the contractor commits to study within two years replacing its input. This figure is a share of the contract value. It is not the 35 % component cost threshold above.

rules.title: AQAP quality certification
rules.reason: AQAP 2110 (or 2310 for aviation and space) is required where a NATO or national contract names it. This service cannot know which of your target contracts do.
rules.note: For Spain this is stated in a primary source: the Ministry of Defence says the PECAL, based on the AQAP, specify the quality requirements that suppliers must meet in the defence contracts that include them (read on 20 October 2026; rule ES-PECAL-CONTRACT of the Spanish defence supplier route, verified). For other countries it rests on the research notes.

source.text: [DefenceGate technical appendix, AQAP editions and who requires it] AQAP enters through individual contracts: when a prime or a national buyer names it, and it then cascades down the supply chain to subcontractors.

rules.title: AQAP editions as the Spanish Ministry of Defence lists them
rules.reason: When a contract names an AQAP or a PECAL, check the edition. The Ministry of Defence lists: PECAL 2110 Ed. 4 = AQAP-2110 Ed. D V1; PECAL 2310 Ed. B V1 = AQAP-2310 Ed. B V1; PECAL 2131 Ed. 3 = AQAP-2131 Ed. C V1 (final inspection and test, relevant to build-to-print component makers). PECAL 2210 is a supplement to 2110 or 2310. The contractual AQAP/PECAL 2000 series is a civil standard such as ISO 9001 plus NATO-specific requirements.

source.ref: Ministerio de Defensa, Aseguramiento de la calidad (list of PECAL and AQAP editions)
source.text: [Ministerio de Defensa, Aseguramiento de la calidad] Los requisitos de la serie de normas AQAP/PECAL 2000 contractuales son los requisitos de una norma civil (como por ejemplo, los de la ISO 9001) más una serie de requisitos específicos OTAN.
